nodes.description: The only reported disease-modifying therapy. A severely affected patient who had required tracheostomy and long-term ventilation had sustained immune and pulmonary recovery three years after transplantation. Only one previous transplanted patient had been reported, and no treatment algorithm is established, so this is a documented outcome in two patients rather than a standard of care.

nodes.description: TNF inhibition, IL-12/23 inhibition with ustekinumab, T-cell costimulation blockade with abatacept, methotrexate and B-cell depletion with rituximab were all tried in the patient both reports describe. They are recorded because the negative result is the informative one: none allowed corticosteroids to be tapered, and rituximab caused a severe infusion reaction and hypogammaglobulinemia. That accumulated failure is what the case for transplantation rests on. The modality is OTHER rather than any single platform because the agents span three: monoclonal antibodies (ustekinumab, rituximab, the TNF inhibitors), a fusion protein (abatacept) and a small molecule (methotrexate). They are kept as one record because it is the accumulated failure across all of them, not any one agent, that is the finding.

nodes.description: T cells that should be rendered anergic are not. In the mouse the demonstration is direct and unusually clean: high-dose tolerizing antigen, which normally shuts down the response, fails to block airway inflammation in Itch-null animals. The tolerogenic process that fails is ubiquitination by Itch converging with MEKK1 and JNK signalling. Three further arms contribute in the published mechanism, through JunB-driven Th2 skewing, impaired TGF-beta-driven regulatory T cell generation, and disinhibited NF-kappaB signalling; those are not separately curated here because the entry's sources demonstrate them in mouse and in vitro rather than in patients.

nodes.description: ITCH is a HECT-domain E3 ligase that ubiquitylates and degrades p73, p63, c-Jun, JunB, Notch and c-FLIP, and so sets the level of each. Without it those substrates accumulate. The breadth of the substrate list is why the disease is syndromic rather than purely immunological, and it is what the founding paper means by underscoring the importance of ITCH in many cellular processes.

nodes.description: A cellular energy defect reported in one patient who was originally investigated for a suspected mitochondrial respiratory chain disease. Muscle showed mitochondrial DNA copy number at 57% of controls, and fibroblasts showed reduced fatty acid oxidation, reduced oxidative phosphorylation and reduced ATP production. Whether this contributes to the growth and developmental features, or is a parallel consequence of losing a ligase with many substrates, is not established.

nodes.description: Autoreactive lymphocytes attack liver, gut, lung, thyroid, pancreatic islets, muscle, joints and skin. The involvement accrues over time rather than presenting all at once, which is why a child can be diagnosed with one organ-specific autoimmune disease years before the syndrome is recognised. In the reported liver-failure case the autoimmune manifestations appeared sequentially after a first liver transplant, and the ITCH variant was found only at post-mortem exome sequencing.

nodes.description: The mTOR inhibitor sirolimus, added to existing abatacept, ustekinumab and corticosteroids in the patient both reports describe. The two reports disagree about whether it worked, and the entry records both rather than choosing: the 2022 report describes dramatic improvement in diarrhoea and liver enzymes with reduced inflammation on repeat bowel biopsy, while the 2025 report on the same patient says it was added without much clinical impact. The 2025 report is the later assessment and the one that led to transplantation.
